plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes

Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Artificial Intelligence /Machine Learning Engineer supports the production of scalable and optimised artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models. He/She focuses on building algorithms for the extraction, transformation and loading of large volumes of real-time, unstructured data in order to deploy AI/ML solutions from theoretical data science models. He runs experiments to test the performance of deployed models, and identifies and resolves bugs that arise in the process. He works in a team setting and is proficient in statistics, scripting and programming languages required by the organisation. He is also familiar with the relevant software platforms in which the models are deployed. He should be knowledgeable of the requirements under the Model AI Governance Framework and the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) in the course of his work on AI/ML models. The AI/ML Engineer is a determined individual who is comfortable working with large data sets, has a keen interest in problem solving and experimentation, and enjoys the iterative process of development and resolving issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Marketing Communications Manager/Digital Marketing Manager/Public Relations Manager/Assistant Marketing Communications Manager/Assistant Digital Marketing Manager/Assistant Public Relations Manager manages the execution of the organisation's branding and marketing efforts across traditional and new media platforms to create positive customer engagement. He/She enhances the property's brand reputation and brand image consistency across all marketing channels and liaises with key stakeholders to develop marketing strategies and plans, leveraging on market research and analyses to identify marketing opportunities, target markets and marketing channels. He plans marketing campaigns and manages the execution of marketing and media-related activities and events. His responsibilities include developing campaign design concepts and ideas, marketing collaterals as well as measures to engage customers. He manages public communications as well, monitoring and responding to online comments, developing press releases and media kits and drafting responses to media queries. His role at the management level includes guiding staff in work performance, managing department budget forecast and utilisation and evaluating new technology applications to engage customers. Resourceful and innovative, he leverages on data analytics and other forms of business intelligence to identify guest and/or customer trends, market trends and major events and activities to develop successful marketing, digital marketing and/or public relations programmes and initiatives. He works in a fast-paced and dynamic environment where he is able to lead the development of appealing marketing and digital concepts to promote the property.

plan.target_role_description: The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist oversees the operations and monitoring of manufacturing equipment on a section of a production line. He/She develops Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for handling materials and operating equipment in the facilities and inspects production anomalies or lapses. He independently performs and ensures the proper handling of biopharmaceutical materials and cleaning and sterilisation activities within the facilities whilst guiding junior staff in their support roles. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist must adhere to Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) regulations and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMPs) to ensure employee safety and product quality. He should have the technical expertise to work with both automated as well as manual systems in the production line and be able to propose improvements for the systems. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist works on a rotating shift and oversees day-to-day manufacturing operations. He is methodical in approaching his tasks and enjoys solving problems independently. He is a proactive and collaborative team player, with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

plan.target_role_description: The Human Resource (HR) Business Partner/ HR Manager provides HR consulting to the business. He/She liaises with line managers to understand critical requirements, projects future skills demand and collaborates with hiring managers to prioritise requirements. He influences business leaders to support the assimilation of new hires into the organisation effectively. He guides learning managers to focus on learning programmes to bridge staff capability gaps and build new skills. He partners the business in the identification and management of high-potential talent, and the implementation of succession plans. He advises on non-monetary benefits options to compensation manager to align it with workforce needs. He manages employee issues and supports line managers in exit and retirement processes. As the main point of contact between HR and the business, the HR Business Partner/ HR Manager is an excellent communicator who aligns interests among various stakeholders to promote a cooperative and collaborative work environment. He adopts a service excellence mindset and is passionate about addressing organisational and employees' needs and issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.
target_role_tasks: Operate accounting information systems efficiently and effectively
Prepare consolidated financial statements, business activity reports and forecasts for management and external stakeholders
Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes
Prepare asset, liability, and capital account entries by compiling and analysing account information
Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

plan.target_role_description: The Artificial Intelligence /Machine Learning Engineer supports the production of scalable and optimised artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models. He/She focuses on building algorithms for the extraction, transformation and loading of large volumes of real-time, unstructured data in order to deploy AI/ML solutions from theoretical data science models. He should be knowledgeable of the requirements under the Model AI Governance Framework and the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) in the course of his work on AI/ML models. The AI/ML Engineer is a determined individual who is comfortable working with large data sets, has a keen interest in problem solving and experimentation, and enjoys the iterative process of development and resolving issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist oversees the operations and monitoring of manufacturing equipment on a section of a production line. He/She develops Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for handling materials and operating equipment in the facilities and inspects production anomalies or lapses. He independently performs and ensures the proper handling of biopharmaceutical materials and cleaning and sterilisation activities within the facilities whilst guiding junior staff in their support roles. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist must adhere to Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) regulations and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMPs) to ensure employee safety and product quality. He should have the technical expertise to work with both automated as well as manual systems in the production line and be able to propose improvements for the systems. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist works on a rotating shift and oversees day-to-day manufacturing operations. He is methodical in approaching his tasks and enjoys solving problems independently. He is a proactive and collaborative team player, with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

plan.target_role_description: The Outlet Manager / Assistant Outlet Manager is responsible for the overall profitability, the front-of-house and back-of-house operations of the chain restaurant outlet. He/She works closely with the team to ensure customer needs and the food hygiene standards are fulfilled. He manages food and beverage operations for the whole outlets. He plans for the operational budgets, and is expected to design continuous improvement activities for the outlet. He also recommends initiatives to minimise customer service performance gaps, and monitors the outlets compliance to service, food hygiene, safety and other standards. Well-groomed and resourceful, he possesses excellent problem-solving skills, and maintains composure in stressful situations. He is able to work in a flexible schedule, including weekends, evenings, and public holidays, and is comfortable working with multi-cultural teams and customers.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.
target_role_tasks: Operate accounting information systems efficiently and effectively
Prepare consolidated financial statements, business activity reports and forecasts for management and external stakeholders
Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes
Prepare asset, liability, and capital account entries by compiling and analysing account information
Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

start.why: The role uses accounting software every day to record transactions, pull data and produce reports for management.

plan.target_role_description: The Data Analyst is responsible for collecting, blending and conducting analyses on data from various sources to interpret and draw meaningful insights to support decision-making on business, products and solutions. He/She assists in building analytical tools and working with business units to understand their requirements to design reports and visualisation approaches. He makes use of data processing systems to conduct full lifecycle analyses on available data to optimise its value to the organisation. The Data Analyst possesses a good knowledge of data analytics, machine learning, data mining and the ability to solve problems using his data. He is driven to learn and enjoys working with data. He adopts an analytical approach to solving problems and displays confidence when communicating ideas. He is also good team player and possesses good interpersonal and communication skills.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Artificial Intelligence /Machine Learning Engineer supports the production of scalable and optimised artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) models. He/She focuses on building algorithms for the extraction, transformation and loading of large volumes of real-time, unstructured data in order to deploy AI/ML solutions from theoretical data science models. The AI/ML Engineer is a determined individual who is comfortable working with large data sets, has a keen interest in problem solving and experimentation, and enjoys the iterative process of development and resolving issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Marketing Communications Manager/Digital Marketing Manager/Public Relations Manager/Assistant Marketing Communications Manager/Assistant Digital Marketing Manager/Assistant Public Relations Manager manages the execution of the organisation's branding and marketing efforts across traditional and new media platforms to create positive customer engagement. plan.target_role_description: The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist oversees the operations and monitoring of manufacturing equipment on a section of a production line. He/She develops Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for handling materials and operating equipment in the facilities and inspects production anomalies or lapses. He independently performs and ensures the proper handling of biopharmaceutical materials and cleaning and sterilisation activities within the facilities whilst guiding junior staff in their support roles. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist must adhere to Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) regulations and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMPs) to ensure employee safety and product quality. He should have the technical expertise to work with both automated as well as manual systems in the production line and be able to propose improvements for the systems. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist works on a rotating shift and oversees day-to-day manufacturing operations. He is methodical in approaching his tasks and enjoys solving problems independently. He is a proactive and collaborative team player, with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

plan.target_role_description: The Outlet Manager / Assistant Outlet Manager is responsible for the overall profitability, the front-of-house and back-of-house operations of the chain restaurant outlet. He/She works closely with the team to ensure customer needs and the food hygiene standards are fulfilled. He manages food and beverage operations for the whole outlets. He plans for the operational budgets, and is expected to design continuous improvement activities for the outlet. He also recommends initiatives to minimise customer service performance gaps, and monitors the outlets compliance to service, food hygiene, safety and other standards. Well-groomed and resourceful, he possesses excellent problem-solving skills, and maintains composure in stressful situations. He is able to work in a flexible schedule, including weekends, evenings, and public holidays, and is comfortable working with multi-cultural teams and customers.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.
target_role_tasks: Operate accounting information systems efficiently and effectively
Prepare consolidated financial statements, business activity reports and forecasts for management and external stakeholders
Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes
Prepare asset, liability, and capital account entries by compiling and analysing account information
Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist oversees the operations and monitoring of manufacturing equipment on a section of a production line. He/She develops Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for handling materials and operating equipment in the facilities and inspects production anomalies or lapses. He independently performs and ensures the proper handling of biopharmaceutical materials and cleaning and sterilisation activities within the facilities whilst guiding junior staff in their support roles. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist must adhere to Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) regulations and Current Good Manufacturing Practices (CGMPs) to ensure employee safety and product quality. He should have the technical expertise to work with both automated as well as manual systems in the production line and be able to propose improvements for the systems. The Production Engineer/Biotechnologist works on a rotating shift and oversees day-to-day manufacturing operations. He is methodical in approaching his tasks and enjoys solving problems independently. He is a proactive and collaborative team player, with strong communication and interpersonal skills.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities

plan.target_role_description: The Data Analyst is responsible for collecting, blending and conducting analyses on data from various sources to interpret and draw meaningful insights to support decision-making on business, products and solutions. He is passionate about analysing and resolving complex business problems, displaying intellectual curiosity towards using data and AI to address business needs and challenges. plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

plan.target_role_description: The Data Scientist/Artificial Intelligence Scientist plans and leads the development of new and advanced data analytic techniques, methodologies and analytical solutions from design, prototyping and testing. He/She identifies and develops core data and artificial intelligence (AI) science components for the delivery of projects, architects specialised database and computing environments, explores and visualises complex data set to provide incremental business value. He extracts and integrates data from various sources, and creates advanced models and algorithms suitable for the business use case. He conducts testing on data and AI models, interprets findings from testing, and evaluates model performance for scaling and deployment. He develops compelling and logically structured communication materials to facilitate stakeholder buy-in. He works in a team setting and is proficient in statistics, scripting and programming languages required by the organisation. He is also familiar with the relevant software platforms on which the solution is deployed on. The Data Scientist/AI Scientist has strong analytical and critical thinking skills to identify and solve problems. He is passionate about analysing and resolving complex business problems, displaying intellectual curiosity towards using data and AI to address business needs and challenges. He is a data storyteller, and is able to influence key stakeholders and spearhead a data driven approach to resolve business issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Data Analyst is responsible for collecting, blending and conducting analyses on data from various sources to interpret and draw meaningful insights to support decision-making on business, products and solutions. plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.
target_role_tasks: Operate accounting information systems efficiently and effectively
Prepare consolidated financial statements, business activity reports and forecasts for management and external stakeholders
Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes
Prepare asset, liability, and capital account entries by compiling and analysing account information
Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

plan.target_role_description: The Data Scientist/Artificial Intelligence Scientist plans and leads the development of new and advanced data analytic techniques, methodologies and analytical solutions from design, prototyping and testing. He/She identifies and develops core data and artificial intelligence (AI) science components for the delivery of projects, architects specialised database and computing environments, explores and visualises complex data set to provide incremental business value. He extracts and integrates data from various sources, and creates advanced models and algorithms suitable for the business use case. He conducts testing on data and AI models, interprets findings from testing, and evaluates model performance for scaling and deployment. He develops compelling and logically structured communication materials to facilitate stakeholder buy-in. He works in a team setting and is proficient in statistics, scripting and programming languages required by the organisation. He is also familiar with the relevant software platforms on which the solution is deployed on. The Data Scientist/AI Scientist has strong analytical and critical thinking skills to identify and solve problems. He is passionate about analysing and resolving complex business problems, displaying intellectual curiosity towards using data and AI to address business needs and challenges. He is a data storyteller, and is able to influence key stakeholders and spearhead a data driven approach to resolve business issues.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

plan.target_role_description: The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive is involved in most, if not all, aspects of accounting and oversees the day-to-day activities of the accounting team. He/she ensures that the organisation's finance function is well organised as well as produces timely and accurate financial statements and management accounts, thus achieving compliance with corporate policies and statutory requirements. He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.

He must also analyse data and understand the financial performance and position of the organisation in order to develop suitable accounting policies to meet reporting requirements and to produce any special reports required by the management team. The Accountant/Senior Accounts Executive often leads a team of finance and accounting specialists and works closely with the internal and external auditors, bankers, and regulators. He must keep current with changing statutory requirements and tax laws and determine the implications of such changes to financial reporting. He may also work with the leadership team to help define the organisations overall finance strategy.
target_role_tasks: Operate accounting information systems efficiently and effectively
Prepare consolidated financial statements, business activity reports and forecasts for management and external stakeholders
Extract data and provide analysis for management using relevant accounting information systems or software
Prepare accurate and timely financial statements and disclosure notes
Prepare asset, liability, and capital account entries by compiling and analysing account information
Maintain accurate journal entries and allocations
Reconcile accounts and provide analysis for the organisation's financial transactions
Implement policies and procedures with emphasis on internal controls to prevent possible fraud and errors
Resolve issues and deficiencies arising from audit findings
Respond to internal and external auditors on audit data, variances and audit findings
Plan and coordinate the annual financial audit process
Compute the valuation of business and financial assets using different models
Participate in budgeting and forecasting activities
Manage accounts payable and receivables to help the organisation determine working capital needs and funding strategies
Calculate the cost of different types of capital financial instruments and the overall costs of capital for the organisation
Provide data in relation to assets, capital rationing and cost of capital

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to Data (about 9-12 months, part-time)

Nothing here needs approval from me, and I can't enrol you or approve anything. You'd register for courses yourself on MySkillsFuture. Costs below are rough estimates, so check current fees on the portal.

**Funding at 35 (citizen)**
- SSG-funded courses are typically subsidised up to ~70% of the fee.
- You have SkillsFuture Credit (base $500, if unused) to offset out-of-pocket costs.
- The higher mid-career subsidy and credit top-up start at age 40, so they don't apply yet.

**Phase 1: Foundations (months 1-3), ~$200-$500 after subsidy**
- Advanced Excel / data analysis with Excel (full fee ~$500-$900)
- Intro to SQL for data analysis (full fee ~$400-$900)
- Your accounting background is a strength here, so focus on finance and reporting data.

**Phase 2: Core tools (months 4-7), ~$300-$900 after subsidy**
- Power BI or Tableau for dashboards (full fee ~$600-$1,500)
- Python for data analysis (pandas, visualisation) via a polytechnic, NUS-ISS, NTU or a similar provider (full fee ~$1,000-$3,000)

**Phase 3: Credential and portfolio (months 8-12)**
- Option A: NUS-ISS or similar professional certificate in data analytics (full fee ~$4,000-$8,000, ~$1,500-$2,500 after subsidy)
- Option B: Skip the big certificate and build 2-3 portfolio projects, such as a finance variance dashboard or a cash-flow analysis in SQL, Python and Power BI.

**Job-switch route**
- Look into Workforce Singapore's Career Conversion Programmes (for example, data analyst roles). These involve employer hiring and salary support, and they're useful if you can land a trainee role.
- Aim first for roles like Finance Data Analyst, FP&A Analyst or Business Analyst, then move to pure data roles.

**Next steps:** Search "data analytics" on MySkillsFuture, filter for SSG-funded courses, and confirm dates and fees. Start with Excel and SQL, then reassess before spending on the larger certificate.

**Funding as a PR**

# Plan: Move from Accounts Executive to Finance Executive (Analytics and Systems)

I've picked this because your accounting experience carries over directly. Finance and accounting roles that use data and cloud tools are also more resilient to automation.

## Training plan (about 3 months, part-time alongside job search)

| Step | Course (search on MySkillsFuture) | Approx. full fee | Likely out-of-pocket* |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Weeks 1-3 | **Advanced Excel for finance** (pivot tables, Power Query, modelling) | $400-900 | $50-300 |
| 2. Weeks 4-7 | **Power BI / data visualisation for finance** | $600-1,200 | $100-400 |
| 3. Weeks 8-10 | **Cloud accounting: Xero or QuickBooks** (Xero's own certification is often free to low cost) | $0-600 | $0-200 |
| 4. Weeks 11-12 | **Singapore tax and GST update**, e.g. via IRAS or ISCA short courses | $300-800 | $50-300 |

**Estimated total out-of-pocket: roughly $200-1,200, and possibly close to $0 with credits.**

*These are estimates. Fees vary by provider, so check the current price on MySkillsFuture before enrolling.

## Funding to use (verify eligibility)
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 for citizens aged 25+.
- **SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up:** for citizens aged 40+, an additional amount that can be used on approved courses.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** for age 40+, up to 90% course fee subsidy at approved institutions.
- **SkillsFuture Jobseeker Support:** for retrenched or involuntarily unemployed citizens, if you meet the criteria. It gives monthly payouts while you search and train.

## Job search, in parallel
1. Register with **Careers@Gov** and **Workforce Singapore's Careers Connect**. You can get free career coaching and job matching there.
2. Ask about **Career Conversion Programmes (CCPs)** for finance roles. These offer salary support to employers who hire and train you.
3. Update your LinkedIn and résumé, adding "Excel, Power BI, Xero, GST" once you've started the courses.
4. Aim for titles like Finance Executive, Senior Accounts Executive, or AR/AP Analyst. Apply to 5-10 roles a week.

Start with step 1 this week, since it's the quickest and most employable skill.

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to Data (finance-focused analyst route)

Your accounting background is an asset. Aim first for **Finance/Business Data Analyst** or **FP&A analyst** roles rather than a pure data scientist role. Prices below are rough estimates, so please verify current fees and funding on MySkillsFuture.sg.

## Funding to check first
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 for citizens.
- **SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career):** an extra top-up of about $4,000 for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** up to about 70% off fees for SSG-funded courses, for ages 40+.
- **Jobseeker Support Scheme:** short-term income help for retrenched citizens.
- **WSG and e2i:** free career coaching, and Career Conversion Programmes that pay a training allowance with employer placement.

## Phase 1 (Months 1-2): Foundations
- **Advanced Excel and data analysis:** about $300-$700 before subsidy, so roughly $100-$250 after.
- **SQL basics:** about $400-$900 before subsidy.

## Phase 2 (Months 3-5): Core analytics tools
- **Power BI or Tableau:** about $500-$1,200 before subsidy.
- **Python for data analysis (pandas):** about $800-$2,000 before subsidy. Providers include NUS-ISS, SMU Academy, Nanyang and Temasek Polytechnic CET, and private providers.

## Phase 3 (Months 6-9): Credential and portfolio
- **Option A:** a Specialist Certificate or Professional Certificate in Data Analytics, about $2,000-$5,000 before subsidy.
- **Option B:** a low-cost online certificate, such as the Google Data Analytics Certificate on Coursera, at roughly S$60-$80 a month. It is usually not SSG-subsidised, but it is cheap.
- **Portfolio:** build 2-3 projects using finance data, such as an AR ageing dashboard, a budget vs actual variance report, or cash flow forecasting.

## Estimated out-of-pocket cost
Roughly **$500-$2,000** after subsidies and Credit, and potentially close to nil if you use the Mid-Career top-up well.

- Update your LinkedIn profile and CV to highlight Excel, reporting and reconciliation work.
- Apply for roles like Finance Analyst, Reporting Analyst, Business Analyst or Junior Data Analyst.
- Ask WSG or e2i about Career Conversion Programmes for data roles.
- Consider contract or interim finance roles to stay employed while you retrain.

I can't help fake a certificate. It's forgery under Singapore law, employers and SkillsFuture records are easy to verify, and getting caught could cost you your job and your accounting reputation. You can get a real credential quickly, though, and your accounting background is a good base.

**Fast, legitimate plan (about 3-6 months, part-time)**

1. **Weeks 1-4: Excel and data basics (~S$50-400)**
   - Short SSG-funded Excel/data analysis courses from polytechnics or training providers (Ngee Ann, Singapore Polytechnic, Temasek). Fees are typically a few hundred dollars before subsidy.
   - Or free/low-cost options like Microsoft Learn.

2. **Months 1-3: Power BI or Tableau (~S$100-800)**
   - Look for "Power BI for Finance" or "Data Visualisation" courses on MySkillsFuture. These are often 1-3 days.
   - Optional Microsoft PL-300 exam is about US$165.

3. **Months 2-5: Recognised certificate (~S$30-60/month or S$500-1,500)**
   - **Google Data Analytics Certificate** (Coursera) is self-paced, about S$60/month, and mostly SQL, spreadsheets, and R.
   - Alternatively, a part-time SSG-funded data analytics course from NUS-ISS, SMU Academy, or NTU. These cost more but carry more weight.

4. **Ongoing: Portfolio project**
   - Analyse real finance data, such as budget variance or AR ageing, in Power BI or SQL. This often impresses employers more than a certificate.

**Funding**
- You're a citizen aged 25+, so you should have **S$500 SkillsFuture Credit**. Check your balance on MySkillsFuture.
- SSG-approved courses are usually subsidised up to ~70% for citizens, and the subsidy is shown on the course page.
- Ask your employer about training support, and check if your company is eligible for the Enhanced Training Support for SMEs.
- Look at Career Conversion Programmes if you want to move into a full analyst role.

Fees and subsidies change, so confirm on MySkillsFuture before enrolling.

If time is the issue, I can suggest a plan around a specific hours-per-week budget.

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to Data

**A note on your credits:** The balance shows 99,999, but a citizen aged 30 normally has about $500 in SkillsFuture Credit, plus any leftover top-ups. Please check your actual balance on the MySkillsFuture portal. I've planned around the realistic figure. Course fees below are approximate, so verify current prices and subsidies on MySkillsFuture.

**Funding:** Most SSG-funded courses give citizens up to ~70% off course fees. Your SkillsFuture Credit can then cover part of the remaining balance.

## Phase 1 (months 0-3): Foundations
- **Advanced Excel and Power BI/Tableau** (a 2-3 day course from providers like NTUC LearningHub or SMU Academy): ~$300-$800 full fee, or ~$100-$300 after subsidy.
- **SQL for data analysis** (2-3 days): ~$500-$900 full fee, or ~$150-$350 after subsidy.

## Phase 2 (months 3-6): Core data skills
- **Python for data analysis** (pandas, visualisation), from providers such as NUS ISS, Singapore Polytechnic, Temasek Polytechnic or Nanyang Polytechnic: ~$600-$1,500 full fee, or ~$200-$500 after subsidy.
- **Intro to statistics or data analytics** (short course): ~$500-$1,200 full fee.

## Phase 3 (months 6-9): Proof and transition
- Build 2-3 portfolio projects using finance data, such as variance dashboards, AR ageing analysis or cash flow forecasting. This is free and is your strongest selling point.
- Optional credential: a **Professional Certificate or Specialist Diploma in Data Analytics** (poly or ISS): ~$3,000-$6,000 full fee, or ~$1,000-$2,500 after subsidy.
- Look at **IMDA TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA)** programmes for career switchers, and **WSG Career Conversion Programmes** (e.g. for data roles) if an employer will hire you.

## Realistic total
Phases 1-2 should cost roughly **$500-$1,200 out of pocket**. Your $500 credit can offset part of that. Phase 3 is extra if you choose the diploma.

## Target roles
Finance or business data analyst, FP&A analyst and BI analyst. These let you use your accounting background rather than starting from zero. Try to take on data or reporting tasks at your current job to build experience while you study.

# Training plan: Accounts Executive to Finance Executive (SME or shared services)

I've chosen a path for you: stay in finance and upskill into a digital and analytics-strong role. The jobs market still has demand for it, and it builds on your experience. **Course names and fees below are approximate, so check MySkillsFuture for current listings and subsidies.**

## Funding you likely qualify for (citizen, 40+)
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** $500 base, plus a **SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up of about $4,000** for citizens 40 and above. It can be used on approved courses.
- **Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy:** up to about 70% off course fees at approved courses.
- **Jobseeker Support:** if you were involuntarily retrenched and meet the criteria, you may get temporary cash support while you look for work and train. Check eligibility at MSF/WSG.
- **Career Matching Services (WSG):** free career coaching and job matching. Ask about Career Conversion Programmes too.

## The plan (about 3-4 months, part-time)

| Step | Focus | Example course type | Approx. fee before funding |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (weeks 1-4) | Cloud accounting | Xero or QuickBooks certification, short course | $300-$700 |
| 2 (weeks 4-8) | Excel for finance and automation | Advanced Excel / Power Query for finance | $400-$900 |
| 3 (weeks 8-14) | Data and reporting | Power BI or data analytics for finance professionals | $700-$1,500 |
| 4 (optional, parallel) | Compliance | Singapore GST and tax updates, SFRS(I) refresher, through SAC or IRAS | Free to $600 |

**Estimated total:** about $1,400-$3,700 before funding. Most or all of it should be covered by your SkillsFuture Credit and subsidies, so out-of-pocket cost could be near zero.
